sourceInformation.source: Cosmic Ark (1982), designed by Rob Fulop and published by Imagic for Atari 2600.
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 3D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; bundled using esbuild 0.25.12.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded / ink illustration, faceted 3D dioramas, bold outlines and printed star-chart details.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and keyframe clips for creatures and machinery, with procedural flight, beams, particles and transitions.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated adaptive synth music (10% by default), effects, and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world co-op for 1–4 players; standalone BroadcastChannel local link for 1–4 same-browser tabs; shared helm and shared rescue cargo.
sourceInformation.testing: 157 checks passed: 20 native-physics/gameplay checks including complete campaign playthroughs, 21 scene/animation checks, 98 browser checks, 9 transport checks and 9 package/metadata checks. Browser coverage includes keyboard/mouse, emulated standard gamepad, multitouch, finite offline audio PCM, local-link co-op, direct file:// launch, and all four official AI Hub scenarios (53 individual conformance assertions). Screenshots used only for visual review. Physical controller and real iPhone/iPad validation: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original 1982 instruction manual (AtariAge), original AtariAge screenshots, archived contemporary review describing sound, and official AI Hub protocol. Three.js and Rapier documentation consulted.

testingFeedback: 4 game issues found by automated and visual testing (2 physics/rescue, 2 visual), all corrected; one additional failed check was a touch-test selector error and was corrected in the test.
1 game-breaking issue: clearing a pending sentry warning could try to remove a nonexistent rigid body. Fixed and covered by regression tests.
The complete scripted campaign using real Rapier collisions, plus the official AI Hub harness with four players, latency/loss, host departure and a dedicated server.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank on this environment; state checks verified WebGPU, and the renderer’s WebGL backend supplied useful visual screenshots.
engineFeedback: Three.js scene graphs, native AnimationMixer and WebGPURenderer made procedural characters and animation straightforward.
Headless WebGPU rendered but its screenshot was blank; the WebGL backend was used for visual inspection.
The alternating rescue/defense campaign, controller-first UI, synth audio and authoritative multiplayer game state.
Coordinating Rapier sensor lifetimes, phase transitions and the asynchronous multiplayer lifecycle.
A reliable headless WebGPU screenshot path.
promptFeedback: The source research requirement and the detailed controller, attract-mode and testing expectations.
The meaning of standalone online was open; AI Hub provides cross-device networking, while standalone local link is explicitly same-device tabs.
Combining a polished single-file game with all input modes and the complete multiplayer lifecycle.
Make the expected standalone networking scope explicit.

aiHub.name: Cosmic Hitchhikers
aiHub.tagline: Six little lives. One last flight.
aiHub.description: Defend a rescue ark through meteor storms, then fly down to three strange worlds and beam the last pairs of beasties aboard. Save all six and weather a final escape, alone or with a shared-helm crew.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick: aim/fire in space, fly on planets; Space/Cross/A: beam; Shift/Circle/B: pulse; mouse: aim/fire or click a beastie; Esc/Options: pause; touch: drag to fly, assisted beam/aim.
